decisions.executionNote: Raise right arm and begin a continuous elbow-up approach toward the basket; keep left parked.
Move above the basket's rear-right egg while rotating the right fingers downward; monitor IK continuity.
Align open fingers over the rear-right egg and descend cautiously; estimate link6-to-grasp offset from views.
Lower a small amount around the rear-right egg and close the right gripper; retention still unconfirmed.
Maintain closure and perform a short vertical retention test before transfer.
Egg was not retained. Reopen and correct the grasp toward the rear-right egg, lowering further around its sides.
Close around the now-centered egg, then lift a few centimeters to verify retention.
Egg appears between the fingers. Lift clear and begin moving toward the holder with a gentle inward tilt, keeping the right elbow configuration.
Carry the retained egg toward the holder's rear-right cup, keeping the right link6 on its side and lowering gradually.
Holder lid closed during transfer and egg retention is uncertain. Clear right hand upward; start a left-side approach to reopen the lid.
Approach the holder's front latch with the left arm, rotating downward while the right hand clears to its own side.
Position the left open gripper over the front lid tab to reopen the holder; right hand remains clear.
Left fingers contacted the lid side. Lift clear before centering over the front tab for an opening grasp.
Use smaller lift increments and a slight orientation correction after the continuity rejection; clear the lid edge.
Move above the front center of the closed lid with clearance, keeping the left arm in its workspace.
Tracking suggests contact at the lid edge. Lift the left gripper straight clear before repositioning.
Translate the raised left hand over the front lid tab, staying left of the centerline.
Lower the left open fingertips toward the front lip of the lid for a cautious reopening grasp.
Test a light front-edge lid grasp with the left gripper, then lift slightly to check whether the lid follows.
The lid did not follow. Reopen and lower the left fingertips toward the actual front lip height.
Contact prevents further descent. Move outside the front rim before attempting to catch the lid lip.
Lower outside the front rim, pinch the lid lip, and test lifting it without moving the base.
Continue a small upward/backward lid-opening test with the left grip closed, checking the lid motion visually.
Reorient the left gripper for an angled front-lip approach rather than descending onto the lid surface.
Bring the angled left fingertips down outside the front edge, avoiding pressure on the lid top.
Align with the visible front latch, close the left fingers, and lift to test reopening.
The lid has started opening. Continue the upward and rearward motion to move it clear of the cups.
Lid is open again. Clear the left hand and approach the basket's front-right egg from above with the right gripper.
Lower the right fingers around the centered front egg while withdrawing the left hand further clear.
Center on the front egg, close fully, and test a short lift; check retention from the next views.
The front egg remains in the basket. Reopen and lower the grasp closer to its equator before closing again.
Correct toward the front egg seen below the finger tips, relieving contact rather than forcing further descent.
Replan from the interrupted pose. Close around the central egg currently between the jaws and lift vertically to test retention.
Use a small orientation bridge after the continuity rejection, close the fingers, and lift clear of basket contact.
Clear the rim and switch to a vertical approach over the rear-right egg, since the front grasp has not retained an egg.
Center the rear-right egg between the open fingers during a slow vertical descent, away from the front basket rim.
Close around the centered rear-right egg while lowering a few millimeters, then test a short lift.
Egg slipped toward the basket center. Recenter and approach deeper with a narrower open grip to avoid the rim.
Use the wrist view to move the fingers toward the egg below the current grasp line, then close and test retention.
The egg is now between the fingers. Lift vertically with the grip closed to confirm retention and clear the rim.
Egg is visibly retained. Raise it well above the open lid and move toward the front-right cup, with a small inward tilt.
Align the retained egg above the holder's front-right cup at safe height, keeping right link6 on the right.
Lower the retained egg toward the front-right cup, correcting slightly inward and rearward while keeping the lid clear.
Seat the egg lower over the front-right recess, then open the gripper and inspect the placement.
Withdraw open fingers from the seated egg and lift clear before approaching another egg.
First egg remains seated. Approach the middle remaining egg from above with nearly vertical fingers.
Adjust rearward and slightly left over the middle egg, lowering the pads to its sides.
Align over the rear-left egg now visible nearest the pads, close fully, and make a short retention test.
Lift straight up with the right grip closed and check whether the second egg remains between the pads.
The rear egg was not retained. Reopen and shift rearward to center it between the pads before a deeper grasp.
Narrow the open grip to clear the basket wall, center slightly right and rearward on the egg, then close and test a small lift.
The second egg appears between the pads. Lift it clear of the basket while keeping the grip closed and check retention.
The second egg slipped. Reapproach with the egg deeper between the finger pads rather than at their tips, correcting rearward.
Narrow to clear the basket wall, lower around the rear egg, and close with the egg deeper between the pads.
Correct toward the actual rear egg using the head view; lower the open pads without closing above empty space.
Shift the pads forward toward the egg visible below the wrist grasp line, then close around its sides and test a small lift.
Lift slowly with the grip closed to verify whether the egg stays between the pads before transfer.
Recenter over the leftmost remaining egg after it rolled forward, lowering open fingers around its sides.
The egg is centered between the pads. Close at this depth and lift gently to verify the grasp.
Lift the retained second egg clear and start moving toward the rear-right holder cup with a gentle inward tilt.
Carry the second egg above the rear-right cup, keeping it above the lid before beginning a vertical descent.
Lower the second egg vertically over the rear-right recess with a small leftward correction; retain full closure.
Contact is limiting descent near the lid. Release the egg above the aligned rear-right cup, then withdraw upward and rightward.
Two eggs appear seated. Clear the lid and move above the rightmost remaining egg, returning the fingers to a vertical approach.
Descend over the rightmost remaining egg with a partly open gripper to clear the basket rim.
Close around the centered third egg with a small forward correction, then lift gently to test retention.
Lift the third egg to verify retention, then begin a gentle inward transfer without crossing the arm links.
The third egg slipped back. Return with a narrower vertical grasp and lower the pads farther around the egg.
Center the rightmost egg deeper between the pads, close fully, and perform a short vertical retention test.
Lift the third egg vertically with the grip closed and verify that it stays between the pads before transfer.
Third egg is retained. Lift and transfer toward the empty front-left cup, tilting inward while keeping right link6 on its own side.
Align the held third egg over the front-left cup with inward fingertip reach; keep both arm links separated.
Lower the third egg toward the front-left recess, with a small rearward correction and continued closed grip.
